mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant above 5.25% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return is expected to be negative due to persistent higher real borrowing costs depressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05), or the Fed cuts rates within 90 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which tends to boost investor confidence and drive positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 out of 30 instances meeting the trigger, the SPX 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect size is smaller than the historical average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return as it reflects stronger consumer demand and near-term economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 such triggers, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is smaller than the median positive return from similar past cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month is associated with a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals supply-side weakness and potential recessionary pressure.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: In 8 such contraction months, the SPX 20-day forward return is not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the average return magnitude does not exceed historical supply contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be negative due to anticipated inflationary pressure and rate hike anticipation.
failure_condition: Across 12 such episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05), or the average return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in job openings (not directly observable in the catalog, so this sketch uses only UNRATE and PAYEMS as proxies) suggests a tight labor market, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.1 percentage points AND PAYEMS increases month-over-month
failure_condition: In 15 such triggered months, the SPX 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect size is smaller than the 95th percentile of prior tight-labor periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months, despite no change in consumer demand proxies (HOUST), predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals weakening overall economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months AND HOUST remains flat or increases for the same two months
failure_condition: Over 8 such double-month contractions, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the average return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of declining consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as markets anticipate the Fed may hold rates steady or cut rates, improving equity valuations.
failure_condition: In 12 such three-month deflationary periods, the SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is smaller than the median positive return from prior deflationary windows.
